subject: Aegis procurement acceptance headers, invoice rail and net-term proposal
body:
From: Oliver White <oliver.white@aegishealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@aegishealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO acceptance format + net terms question

Jordan —

Thanks for the quote attached to the portal. Procurement asked for a couple quick clarifications before we can issue a PO: 1) the PO needs to include a tax id / remit address line (their template attached); 2) they want to confirm net terms — they usually operate on Net 60 for SaaS vendors, but Finance asked whether Redwood can accept Net 30 or if there is a standard Net 45 option; and 3) they prefer consolidated monthly invoices rather than sending a separate invoice per engagement.

Can you confirm acceptance of the PO template fields and whether any pricing/discount changes if we move to Net 60 + monthly consolidated invoices? We also have a small internal requirement to list a contract reference on the PO (field: Contract Ref).

Thanks,
Oliver
Procurement Manager | Aegis Health

Attachment: Aegis_PO_Template.pdf (PDF, 92KB)

----

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Oliver White <oliver.white@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO acceptance format + net terms question

Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the template. Quick answers up front: Redwood can populate Tax ID, Remit Address, and a Contract Ref on the invoice/PO acknowledgement. We normally price and discount on a Net 30 baseline, but we do have flexibility for enterprise customers on Net terms and consolidated billing. A few clarifying questions to make sure procurement and finance are aligned:

- Is Aegis asking for monthly consolidated invoices for all Redwood usage under the contract, or consolidated per legal entity / BU?
- Is Net 60 a hard requirement from their AP policy, or would they accept Net 45 if there are concessions to pricing?
- Are they expecting advance PO values (commitments) or will POs be issued per billing period with a running PO reference?

Ben — can you outline the commercial impact if we move to Net 60 + monthly consolidated invoices vs Net 30 + per-engagement invoicing?
Vanessa — any operational caveats on our side for monthly consolidated statements (ledger tags, PO matching accuracy)?
Kimberly — any legal concerns listing Contract Ref and soft acceptance window in PO ack?

I attached our latest quote (v3) with the current discount bands for a 12-month commitment — I’ll flag the cells that change with term/payment cadence.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Quote-8342-v3.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)

----

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Oliver White <oliver.white@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO acceptance format + net terms question

Oliver / Jordan —

Short version on commercial impact: switching to Net 60 increases credit exposure and working capital needs for Redwood; we typically build that into pricing via either a slightly lower discount or a small finance surcharge for Net 60. For Aegis at the $Xk/month run-rate in quote v3, the typical concession looks like:

- Net 30 + per-engagement invoices: baseline discounts (as in v3).
- Net 45: no change in list price for 12-mo commit; marginal decrease in discount band (~25–50 bps).
- Net 60 + consolidated monthly statements: we can accept, but commercial trade is a 1.5% finance surcharge OR a removal of the largest usage band discount.

That said, if Aegis will sign a 12-month committed ARR and can provide an advance blanket PO (with monthly drawdown reports), we can hold baseline discounts and waive the surcharge. The key is a visible PO commitment number or a pre-funded credit ledger.

If you want I can draft two short options for them: (A) Net 60 + consolidated invoicing with 1.5% surcharge, (B) Net 60 + consolidated invoicing with same price if they pre-fund X months or provide blanket PO coverage.

Ben
Head of Billing & Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference

----

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Oliver White <oliver.white@aegishealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO acceptance format + net terms question

Thanks — operational notes from Redwood’s side:

- We can support consolidated monthly invoices grouped by legal entity. Our billing system accepts a "PO reference" field for each invoice line and can include Contract Ref on header.
- For monthly consolidated statements we need a single master PO per legal entity to match against; multiple POs across BUs will require mapping and may delay matching if PO numbers change frequently.
- If Aegis expects itemized consumption lines, please confirm whether they prefer an aggregated usage summary per product (recommended) or fully itemized hourly token-level detail (possible but will increase statement size and processing latency).
- Attachment: sample consolidated statement layout (we can produce a short sample PDF on request).

Operational impact: monthly statements reduce AP overhead on Aegis but increase reconciliation work for our billing team if POs aren’t stable. If they can lock a master PO for the quarter we can automate 95% of matching.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

----

From: Oliver White <oliver.white@aegishealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO acceptance format + net terms question

Hi team —

Thanks for the quick responses and the options. Procurement confirmed:

- Aegis can provide a master PO per legal entity for the quarter (they prefer quarterly POs due to internal controls).
- Net 60 is their default and they are not able to move to Net 30. Net 45 is negotiable but would require extra approvals and likely delay the PO issuance.
- They are happy with consolidated monthly invoices at legal-entity level and prefer aggregated usage summary rather than full itemization.
- Regarding pre-funding: they can’t pre-fund, but they can provide a committed quarterly PO number with a nominal not-to-exceed amount and monthly drawdowns.

Oliver
Procurement Manager | Aegis Health

----

Notes / next steps (internal):
- Jordan: propose two concise commercial options to present to Aegis: 1) Accept Net 60 + consolidated monthly invoices with 1.5% finance surcharge (no pre-fund), 2) Accept Net 60 + consolidated monthly invoices with baseline pricing if Aegis issues a quarterly master PO with a not-to-exceed commitment (no pre-fund but visible commitment).
- Ben: prepare the short pricing delta table (surcharge vs no surcharge with master PO) and a one-line justification for finance.
- Vanessa: confirm required fields for master PO header and sample consolidated statement PDF; ensure billing automation can map PO -> entity and add Contract Ref on header.
- Kimberly: confirm whether PO header naming convention or Contract Ref wording needs a legal clause in the SOW or contract amendment.

Attachment references: Aegis_PO_Template.pdf; Redwood-Quote-8342-v3.xlsx

----

[End of thread]
